title: Towd (North Sea Wading Place)
summary: Towd is a locality near North Sea in Southampton, described as a cove above a wading place.
history_content: Town records connect Towd with a footpath, stony brook, and later a road leading from the wading place toward Sag Harbor. The modern marker is a general North Sea / Towd Point placement.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Towd, Towde, and Toude. The root is interpreted as to ford or to wade over, while an alternate low-place-between-hills explanation is rejected.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place-names are not only addresses and identities, they are also living stories which have come into existence at different periods in the local people’s past.”

— Botolv Helleland, Place-names and Cultural Heritage (2002), conference paper, PDF page 2
preservation_content: Towd preserves a practical travel name, marking a wading place in the North Sea landscape where paths, coves, and roads met.
